question: The implementation of the Water Framework Directive (WFD) has had profound and unintended consequences on the safeguarding of cultural heritage across several Member States. In particular, the implementation of the legislation has led to a drastic reduction of water flow in certain rivers, thereby causing numerous historical watermills to be abandoned or destroyed because they were no longer able to function.

Although the WFD leaves the responsibility of finding a balance between different objectives (in this case, restoring ecosystems and protecting cultural heritage) to the Member States, the Commission should be able to answer the following questions. 1.
How does it assess the state of affairs concerning watermills following the implementation of the WFD?

Practices put in place to protect cultural heritage under the WFD diverge across Member States. Has the Commission considered creating guidelines and best practices for Member States on how to protect cultural heritage in the context of the WFD? What does it intend to do to ensure that a balanced approach to the WFD is achieved?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.6.2024) The Water Framework Directive (WFD)1 has numerous environmental objectives, notably the principle of non-deterioration of the status of water bodies and the obligation to restore water bodies and achieve good status2.

Its implementation has not led to a drastic reduction of water flows but rather often to the contrary, since it provides for sufficient flow to be kept maintaining or restoring good ecological status.

The Commission has earlier addressed the concerns raised by some Member States regarding the preservation of some water-based heritage, including watermills, although this has not been flagged as an EU-wide-scale problem. As every case is unique and methodologies to classify cultural heritage change from case to case and between Member States, an EU guidance would not necessarily provide the necessary added value.

The Commission encourages the most concerned Member States to improve and enhance the dialogue between water and heritage authorities at national, regional, and local level to find the best solutions for the protection of both sound water management and cultural heritage located along water courses.
1 Directive 2000/60/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2000 establishing a

framework for Community action in the field of water policy, OJ L 327, 22.12.2000, p. 1–73, as amended by Commission Directive 2014/101/EU of 30 October 2014, OJ L 311, 31.10.2014, p. 32–35. 2 Article 4 of WFD.
